messages:
maria_sales: Heads-up — enterprise POC (FinTech customer) needs Dedicated endpoint but they insist on routing traffic through their outbound proxy and doing mTLS on our side. They also want scoped short-lived API keys for the POC. Can we support that without a Private deployment?

alex_solutions: Yes — we can support customer-side proxy + Dedicated in most cases. Two main options: 1) keep Redwood Dedicated endpoint public and require mTLS + IP allowlist; 2) place Dedicated in a Private/VPC peer with a customer NAT/proxy (more setup). For a quick POC I'd recommend 1.

maria_sales: They specifically said they won't allow static IPs in their firewall; they want a small set of certs and ephemeral IPs that rotate daily. Also security wants a mechanism to revoke POC keys instantly.

alex_solutions: For certs: we support mutual TLS to Dedicated endpoints — we can issue a client cert per customer and rotate on request. For ephemeral IPs: we can provision an EIP pool and coordinate rotations, but if the customer refuses any static ranges they need to accept cert-level auth. Short summary:
- mTLS + client certs (recommended)
- Scoped API key + token TTL (we can mint tokens with 1h TTL for POC)
- If they need IP allowlisting only, we need at least a small set of IPs (we can provide 3 rotating EIPs and a rotation window).

sam_security: Important: scoped API keys must be revocable and must not have access to other tenant data. We should create a service-account style key for the POC with a single role: `inference.invoke:limited`. Ensure logs and audit trail are enabled.

alex_solutions: Agreed. Implementation notes:

```
# example: mint short-lived token
POST /v1/tokens
{
  "scopes": ["inference.invoke:limited"],
  "expires_in": 3600
}
```

For mTLS we ask for the customer's CA or they can accept our public client certs. Curl example for testing: `curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://dedicated.us-west-2.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

maria_sales: Customer also needs pricing clarity — are there minimums for a Dedicated pool during POC? They want a 2-week trial without committing to a monthly minimum.

jim_infra: Standard Dedicated has monthly commit tiers but we can do a timeboxed POC with a temporary sandbox Dedicated pool (no long-term commit) — limited throughput and reduced support SLA. Finance needs sign-off but we've done this twice. Estimate: $X for a 2-week sandbox (covers reserved lifecycle & infra). I'll loop in pricing.

alex_solutions: Operational tasks for presales:
- Create POC service account with 1h tokens and a rotation policy.
- Generate client cert for mTLS and provide validation steps.
- If customer allows IPs, offer 3 EIPs + rotation script (we'll share the Terraform snippet).

networking_bot: [automated] Suggested NAT/EIP rotation snippet: `terraform aws_eip.pool[count.index]` + Lambda to rotate and update firewall entries. Link: https://internal.redwood/docs/egress-rotation (internal).

maria_sales: Security questionnaire Q: "Can Redwood revoke client certs and scoped tokens on demand?" How to answer succinctly?

sam_security: Answer: "Yes. Tokens are ephemeral and revocable via the tokens API; client certificates may be revoked by blacklisting their serial in Redwood CA and revoking at the gateway — typical revoke latency < 5 minutes." Add: we capture certificate serials in audit logs.

alex_solutions: I'll prepare a short runbook and a one-page network diagram showing mTLS flow + optional EIP rotation. Also will include the `curl` test and a Postman collection.

maria_sales: Can you estimate lead time for infra work and cert provisioning if they want to start Monday?

alex_solutions: Lead times:
- Service-account + token policy: ~2 business days.
- Client cert issuance + test endpoint: ~1 business day after CA info.
- EIP pool & rotation automation: ~3 business days (if we need to reserve EIPs).

deploy-bot: [provisioning] POC request created: ticket #POC-4512. Assigned to alex_solutions and jim_infra. ETA: see comments.

maria_sales: Great. Last ask — can we limit model selection for the POC (cheaper tokens) and enforce rate limits? They want to avoid unexpected spend.

alex_solutions: Yes — we can pin model family + set per-key rate limits and soft quota. We'll apply a 10k token cap for the POC service account and default lower-performance model to save cost.

jim_infra: I'll draft the quote overlay that shows the sandbox pricing + optional extra for EIP reservation. Will post in this thread by EOD.

maria_sales: Thanks team — I'll schedule a 30-min call with their network/security folks Thursday 3pm PT. Follow-ups: alex to share runbook, jim to post quote, sam to paste the short answer for the questionnaire. :thumbsup:
